# featureflip_flag_environment (Resource)

Per-environment configuration of a feature flag: on/off state, fallthrough, prerequisites, and targeting rules. When `rules` is set it is AUTHORITATIVE: Terraform owns every rule in this flag-environment and removes rules created elsewhere. Import with `<project>/<flag>/<environment>` (imports identifiers only; add rules/prerequisites to config to manage them). Destroying this resource deletes the managed targeting rules and DISABLES the flag in this environment; the fallthrough configuration (default variation/strategy) is left in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "featureflip_flag_environment" "new_checkout_prod" {
  project           = featureflip_project.web.key
  flag              = featureflip_feature_flag.new_checkout.key
  environment       = "production"
  enabled           = true
  default_variation = "false"

  # List position is rule priority. When rules is set, Terraform owns ALL
  # rules in this flag-environment — dashboard-created rules are removed.
  rules = [
    {
      description = "Beta users always get the new checkout"
      variation   = "true"
      segment     = featureflip_segment.beta_users.key
    },
    {
      description        = "50% rollout in Germany"
      variation          = "true"
      rollout_percentage = 50
      condition_groups = [
        {
          operator = "And"
          conditions = [
            { attribute = "country", operator = "Equals", values = ["DE"] },
          ]
        },
      ]
    },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `environment` (String) Environment key.
- `flag` (String) Flag key.
- `project` (String)

### Optional

- `default_variation` (String) Variation KEY served as fallthrough. Defaults to the server-side default when omitted.
- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `prerequisites` (Attributes List) Prerequisite flags. Omit to leave prerequisites unmanaged; set (even empty) to replace wholesale. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--prerequisites))
- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered targeting rules (list position = priority). Authoritative when set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `strategy` (String)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--prerequisites"></a>
### Nested Schema for `prerequisites`

Required:

- `flag` (String) Prerequisite flag key.
- `variation` (String) Expected variation key of the prerequisite flag.


<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `variation` (String) Variation KEY served when the rule matches.

Optional:

- `condition_groups` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--condition_groups))
- `description` (String)
- `rollout_percentage` (Number)
- `segment` (String) Segment KEY this rule targets.

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--rules--condition_groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.condition_groups`

Required:

- `conditions` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--condition_groups--conditions))
- `operator` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--rules--condition_groups--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.condition_groups.conditions`

Required:

- `attribute` (String) User attribute to match, e.g. country or email.
- `operator` (String)
- `values` (List of String)

Optional:

- `negate` (Boolean)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import featureflip_flag_environment.new_checkout_prod web/new-checkout/production
```
